title: SEC confidential-treatment expiry / unsealing information state

hypothesis.mechanism: Public transitions in the confidentiality state of SEC-filed material contracts may reveal information previously withheld from the public, distinct from EDGAR demand, SEC review dialogue, FOIA requests and generic filing complexity.
hypothesis.event_clock: Only the first independently reproducible public SEC observation is eligible; latent expiry is not a tradable clock unless publicly exposed.

evidence_basis.finding: Near confidential-treatment expiry, registrants may refile unredacted exhibits or seek extensions.
Post-2019 redacted-exhibit rules permit certain immaterial competitively harmful redactions; traditional confidential treatment remains available.

evidence_basis.source: Thompson, Urcan & Yoon (2023), The Accounting Review
evidence_basis.finding: Redacted material-contract filings are associated with slower price discovery and greater insider trading.

evidence_basis.source: Kolev, Lee & Neamtiu (2023), Journal of Accounting and Public Policy
evidence_basis.finding: Confidential-treatment requests are associated with more SEC monitoring/comment activity and longer resolution.
The public corpus contains 1,038,766 unique SEC contract URLs from 2000–2023 with filing metadata, document format and amendment status.

cheap_falsifiers: Public archive cannot deterministically reconstruct approval/extension/unredacted-refile lineage.
The useful clock is latent expiry rather than public observation.
Post-2019 regime break prevents valid interpretation.
Event density is too sparse for stable research.
Issuer or contract mapping requires hindsight.
The mechanism collapses to Q218, Q224, Q228 or Q231 under blinded ablation.
status_note: Discovery lead only; not in formal performance candidate registry and carries no performance authorization.
